newsitem.title: UK: Russia sees London Club closing in August.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees London Club closing in August.

text.p: A closing of Russia's London Club arrangements was likely in August if creditors responded promptly to reconciliation statements they have received, deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Tuesday.

"There continues to be significant progress in the reconciliation of Russia's London Club debts. As of today, almost all creditors have received Reconciliation Statements," a statement from the ministry said.
It said that if creditors respond promptly to the statements, "it would be reasonable to foresee a closing of the London Club arrangements in August of this year".
Kasyanov said in March Russia had finished reconciling on $12 billion of the debt.
The minimum necessary sum for closing the London Club rescheduling is $20 billion.
Russia agreed in 1995 with the London Club to reschedule $35 billion in debts inherited from the Soviet Union and interest arrears for up to 25 years.
Reconciliation is the final stage in rescheduling Russia's commercial bank debt, involving checks on all loans included in the agreement.
